resources.string: Local multiplayer · Experimental
LAN connections and shared-screen co-op with Steam Link
Choose LAN play with a game on each device, or shared-screen co-op with one game running on the host. The game must support the chosen multiplayer mode. Device testing is still needed.
Wireless LAN

Host creates a password-protected local network without a router or internet. It may disconnect your current Wi-Fi. On the other device, join using Android Wi-Fi settings and choose to stay connected without internet. For separate-copy LAN games, select the LAN interface below on both devices; for Steam Link, select it on the host only. If cellular takes priority, turn mobile data off while playing.

USB-C / Ethernet LAN

Connect a data-capable USB-C cable and enable USB tethering on one device in Android settings. This only works if the other device supports the USB network driver and host role. If no LAN interface appears, try reversing the cable’s host/device roles or use USB Ethernet adapters. Charging or file-transfer mode alone does not create a LAN. DroidDeck cannot enable USB tethering itself.

Shared-screen co-op · Steam Link

The host runs one copy of a game with local co-op or split-screen support. Both devices see the same picture and each can provide a controller. Steam Link handles the client’s video, audio, and input.
1. Connect both devices to the same Wi-Fi, or create an offline hotspot below and join it from the second device. Select the host’s LAN interface below before starting Steam.

2. On the host, start Steam in DroidDeck, then enable Settings → Remote Play → Enable Remote Play. Keep DroidDeck’s host controls enabled. Return to the host to approve the pairing PIN when Steam Link asks.
Return to host Steam
Back to DroidDeck to start Steam
Selected LAN address: %1$s\nIf discovery fails, add this host address in Steam Link on the second device.
If Steam Link cannot find the host, select the host’s LAN interface below to see its address.

3. On the second device, open Steam Link, pair with the host, and start streaming. Connect that player’s controller to the second device, or enable Steam Link’s touch controller. The second device does not need to run a DroidDeck Linux session.
Open Steam Link on this device
Get Steam Link for this device

4. Launch the game through the host’s Steam and join its local multiplayer mode. Keep the host’s controller and the Steam Link controller as separate gamepads. If both control the same player, check Steam’s controller order and the game’s controller settings. Keyboard and mouse input may be shared instead of creating another player.

Install, sign in, and pair while online before travel. A local hotspot provides the network, but first-time pairing and fully offline Steam Link play still need testing on this setup. No ADB, Shizuku, or root setup is required by this integration.
